rules.rule_en: The Non-Tourist Passenger Baggage Rules, 2025 replace the 2024 rules (SRO 203-Ain/2024/55/Customs). They do not apply to tourists, privileged persons, transit passengers or crew. Customs' FY2026-27 SRO compilation (customs.gov.bd 'All SRO 2026-2027') still cites SRO 261/2025 as the baggage rule, and no newer baggage SRO appears in NBR's June/Aug 2026 budget SRO lists.
Baggage means a reasonable quantity of food, clothing, household or other personal items, with no single item weighing more than 15 kg.
A passenger aged 12 or over arriving by air or sea may clear up to 65 kg of accompanied baggage (hand bag, cabin bag, etc.) free of all duties and taxes.
On top of the 65 kg, up to 35 kg of clothing, personal-use items, books, periodicals and study materials is also duty-free.
A passenger under 12 gets one carton/bag of personal baggage up to 40 kg duty-free and no other benefit; gold/silver bars or ornaments, liquor and the 1 carton of cigarettes are not allowed for them.
rules.figure: 40 kg, one piece; no gold/silver/cigarette/liquor benefit

rules.rule_en: A passenger may bring one of each item in Schedule-3 duty-free and one of each item in Schedule-2 on payment of the fixed duty listed. Extra or other goods (not banned/restricted) are cleared by adjudication with full duty/taxes and an import-control clearance where needed (rule 10).

Schedule-3 duty-free items (one each): desktop/laptop computer with one UPS; computer scanner; printer; non-professional video camera; non-professional still/digital camera; ordinary/electric/microwave oven; rice cooker/pressure cooker/gas oven with burner; toaster/sandwich maker/blender/food processor/juicer/coffee maker; household sewing machine; table/pedestal/ceiling fan; personal sports equipment; gold jewellery up to 100 g and silver jewellery up to 200 g (max 12 of one kind); 1 carton (200 sticks) cigarettes; TV up to 29 inch (Plasma/LCD/TFT/LED/CRT); music centre with CD and 2 speakers; music centre/CD/DVD/Blu-ray player with 4 speakers; 2 used mobile phones; 1 new mobile phone; one carpet up to 15 sq m.

Schedule-2 fixed duty on TVs (Plasma/LCD/TFT/LED): 30-36 inch Tk 10,000; 37-42 inch Tk 20,000; 43-46 inch Tk 30,000; 47-52 inch Tk 50,000; 53-65 inch Tk 70,000; 66 inch and above Tk 90,000. Up to 29 inch is duty-free.

Schedule-2 fixed duty: home theatre/music centre with more than 4 and up to 8 speakers Tk 8,000; refrigerator/deep freezer Tk 5,000; window AC Tk 7,000; split AC up to 18,000 BTU Tk 15,000; split AC above 18,000 BTU Tk 20,000; dish antenna Tk 7,000; professional cameras (HD Cam, DV Cam, BETA Cam, DSLR, mirrorless, interchangeable-lens) Tk 15,000; air gun/air rifle Tk 5,000 (needs Commerce Ministry approval); chandelier Tk 300 per point; dishwasher/washing machine/cloth dryer Tk 3,000.
Anything not for personal/household use, baggage above the rule-3 limits, and any goods in commercial quantity are dutiable (Schedule-2 heads a-c).
One desktop or laptop computer (with one UPS) is duty-free under Schedule-3.
Base 2025 rule: up to 2 used mobile phones, plus 1 new phone once per year, duty-free; phones beyond that fall under rule 10 (full duty by adjudication).

Amendment of 2 July 2025: any passenger may bring 1 new phone per calendar year duty-free; a Bangladeshi expatriate holding a BMET card who has stayed abroad at least 6 months may bring 2 new phones per year duty-free. Same amendment allows online baggage declaration. Only press reports of the SRO were readable; the SRO text itself is not posted on NBR's SRO or baggage-rules pages.
rules.figure: BMET card + 6 months abroad: 2 new phones/year free; others 1 new/year

rules.rule_en: BTRC's NEIR portal lets users register a handset with valid documents and check status by SMS 'KYD <IMEI>' to 16002. A mandatory deadline for registering phones brought from abroad (press reports: 30 days; NEIR rollout targeted 1 Jan 2027) is not stated on an official BTRC page.
Worn or not, a passenger may bring up to 100 g of gold jewellery (22 carat or lower, designed and wearable) duty-free once per year, with a declaration; no more than 12 pieces of one kind.
rules.figure: 100 g/year free, max 12 of a kind

rules.rule_en: Up to 200 g of silver jewellery duty-free once per year with declaration (max 12 pieces of one kind).

Once per year, with declaration, a passenger may bring a gold bar/bullion up to 117 g (10 tola) on payment of fixed duty Tk 5,000 per 11.664 g (1 bhori/tola), i.e. about Tk 50,000 for the full 117 g. Excess or concealed bars are confiscated.
rules.figure: max 117 g (10 tola); Tk 5,000 per 11.664 g; once/year

rules.rule_en: Once per year, with declaration, silver bar/bullion up to 234 g (20 tola) on payment of Tk 6 per 11.664 g. Excess or concealed silver bars are confiscated. Note: the Schedule-1 declaration form text says 200 g silver for bars, conflicting with the 234 g in rule 3(10) and Schedule-2.
rules.figure: max 234 g (20 tola); Tk 6 per 11.664 g; once/year

rules.rule_en: 1 carton (200 sticks) of cigarettes duty-free (not for under-12s).
Foreign passport holders may bring up to 1 litre of liquor/beer duty-free; Bangladeshi passport holders may not import liquor at all.
Portable tools/equipment used for the passenger's profession are duty-free.
Schedule-2/3 items not brought along may be bought within 7 working days of arrival from Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation's city sales centre using the Schedule-4 form.
Passengers arriving by land may bring baggage worth up to USD 400 duty-free, no more than 3 times per calendar year.
Medical equipment and wheelchairs used by sick, disabled or elderly passengers are duty-free.
Baggage of a Bangladeshi citizen who died abroad is exempt from all duties and taxes.
Bangladeshi airline crew returning from duty: baggage up to USD 300 free; Bangladeshi seafarers: USD 300; seafarer on sign-off: up to USD 2,000 on payment of duty.

Unaccompanied baggage: declare on the Schedule-1 form before leaving the customs hall (or within 30 days through an Assistant Commissioner if missed), only once per calendar year, only from the country where the journey started, with booking proof; cleared on payment of duty and taxes. Booked bags that missed the flight are treated as accompanied.
rules.figure: once/year; declare before leaving customs hall

rules.rule_en: All arriving passengers must fill the Schedule-1 baggage declaration form or file it online. Green channel only if nothing dutiable; up to 5% of green-channel passengers may be randomly scanned, and any can be checked on intelligence.
rules.figure: Schedule-1 form / online; 5% random green-channel checks

rules.rule_en: Any amount of foreign currency may be brought in, but amounts above USD 10,000 (or equivalent) must be declared on Form FMJ to Customs on arrival. No declaration needed up to USD 10,000. The USD 5,000 figure in older guides is not in the current rule.
rules.sro: Bangladesh Bank FEPD-1 Circular No. 30 (consolidated import-transactions circular), para 8 'Import of foreign currency notes and coins'

rules.rule_en: An incoming or outgoing passenger may carry up to Tk 10,000 in Bangladesh currency.
rules.sro: Bangladesh Bank FEPD-1 Circular No. 30 (consolidated import-transactions circular), para 8 'Import of foreign currency notes and coins'

rules.rule_en: An arriving person may keep up to USD 10,000 brought in without declaration. A resident Bangladeshi must encash or deposit any excess over USD 10,000 in a foreign-currency account within 30 days; a non-resident Bangladeshi can do so any time.
rules.sro: Bangladesh Bank FEPD-1 Circular No. 30 (consolidated import-transactions circular), para 8 'Import of foreign currency notes and coins'

rules.rule_en: The baggage declaration form asks passengers to report foreign currency above USD 10,000 and to fill the separate FMJ currency form.

Bangladesh Bank gives general permission to adult female incoming passengers to bring any quantity of personal jewellery worn or in personal baggage (foreign-exchange side only; customs limits above still apply).
rules.figure: no FX limit for worn jewellery (adult women)
rules.sro: Bangladesh Bank FEPD-1 Circular No. 30 (consolidated import-transactions circular), para 8 'Import of foreign currency notes and coins'

rules.rule_en: Must be declared at the red channel: banned import goods; meat/dairy/fish/poultry products; seeds, plants, fruit, flowers; gold/silver above the limits; new mobile phones; currency above USD 10,000. All firearms are banned for passengers except an air gun/air rifle (Commerce Ministry approval + Tk 5,000). Goods in commercial quantity and concealed gold are seized. HSIA customs page adds that cigarettes above 1 carton, vapes and liquid nicotine are seized. The full banned-goods list (Import Policy Order) was not compiled here.
rules.figure: declare at red channel; firearms banned
